name: Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.span_kisinLoc
summary: kisinLoc ⊆ kisinLocAinf; conversely M = A_inf·N (frame theorem), and the inverted φ^a E are absorbed by kisinLoc.

steps.claim: The span is contained in kisinLocAinf(L), which contains kisinLoc(L) and is an A_inf-module; for the converse, argue along the saturation:
steps.lean:
span_eq_of_le _ (sep_subset ..) fun _ ↦
    (saturateBy_induction · (frame_theorem.1.2.2.1.trans_le (span_mono fun _ ↦
  .imp_left le_saturateBy)) fun a _ ↦
  (by simpa [← frobEUnit_smul] using
  mapsTo_span (f := k.frobEUnit a ^ (-1) • .id) (fun _ ↦ frobEUnit_zpow_smul_mem_kisinLoc.2) ·))

steps.claim: an element of kisinAinf = M lies in A_inf·N by the frame theorem (M = A_inf N), and N ⊆ kisinLoc;
if φ^a(E)·y is in the span, so is y: multiplication by φ^a(E)^{−1} maps kisinLoc into itself (frobEUnit_zpow_smul_mem_kisinLoc) and so maps the span into itself.
steps.lean:
(by simpa [← frobEUnit_smul] using
  mapsTo_span (f := k.frobEUnit a ^ (-1) • .id) (fun _ ↦ frobEUnit_zpow_smul_mem_kisinLoc.2) ·))
